To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of the metabotropic glutamate receptors is precisely and complex regulated during brain development, and different splice variants of mGlu receptors are likely involved in different functions.
the mGlu5 splice variants are differentially regulated in the brain during development, with mGlu5 a being expressed at higher levels in the adult brain.
the expression of mGluR5b, a splice variant of mGlu receptor 5, is developmentally regulated, with higher expression in developing brain and in the adult cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of metabotropic glutamatergic receptors in synaptic transmission.
the development, expression and function of the mGlu5 splice variants in the brain.
the role of the metabotropic glutamate receptors in the developing and mature nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mGluR5b is a splice variant of mGluR 5 that is highly expressed during development and that the developmental profile of mGlu 5b protein differs from that of mGluS5a.
mGluR5b protein is regulated in a complex manner during development and that the expression of this variant is not simply a reflection of mGluR total expression.
mGluR5b protein is expressed at a higher level than mRNA in most regions, but that the relative levels are different in different brain regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

metabotropic glutamate receptors are highly regulated, but that the splice variants are differentially regulated, and that these differences may be important in the development and function of the brain.
mGluR5 is expressed at high levels in early postnatal development and that this developmental expression is due to the high expression of the mGluR-5a splice variant.
the mGlu5 splice variant 5b is highly regulated during development and in the adult.

mGluR5b is a major component of the mGluR population in the adult brain.
there is a lot more complexity in the expression and regulation of the different variants of mGluRs than we previously appreciated.
